text:
Maya (CEO): thanks for coming to the wrap Q&A. we're getting several hiring/org questions so starting a thread for live follow-ups. drop short questions and we'll answer.
mike_sales (Sales Lead): sales noticed 8 reqs went pending this quarter. should account teams expect slower ramp on AE hires?
Priya (Head of People): sales will proceed but with phased prioritization. quota-bearing roles remain high priority; some SDR/ops reqs were paused to re-evaluate quotas. managers will get a note with specifics by EOD.
Evan (Head of Research): for research hiring  are we still hiring broadly or narrowing to model infra roles?
Jonas (VP Eng): research stays important but we are focusing research hiring on model efficiency and inference optimizations that tie directly to cost/latency wins. general-purpose research reqs are paused for now.
Tess (Hiring Ops): practical note  if you have candidates in pipeline for paused reqs, TA will flag them and discuss alternatives (other teams, contractor conversions). please don't ghost candidates.
mike_sales (Sales Lead): thanks  appreciate that.
Maya (CEO): quick recap of headcount approach: cautious rebuild, align hires with measurable ROI (latency, cost, revenue). we'll target net +6-8% company headcount next year but with rolling approvals.
Jonas (VP Eng): to add on org changes  a small number of teams will consolidate ownership around serving/runtime domains. this is to reduce cross-team dependencies. expect team-level meetings this week if you are affected.
Priya (Head of People): leveling/comp questions: no immediate band changes. we're clarifying titles for senior ICs and creating clearer ladders for TPM/PM. compensation philosophy unchanged.
Evan (Head of Research): curious about internal mobility  if a research engineer wants to move to infra, will they be blocked by headcount constraints?
Priya (Head of People): internal moves prioritized. managers should approve short-term transfers where it helps company priorities; HR will broker approvals so moves don't stall on headcount paperwork.
Tess (Hiring Ops): process change: interview loops for mid-senior ICs will be reduced to 3 interviews + hiring manager convo; detailed rubrics are on Confluence. time-to-offer target set to 28 days.
Jonas (VP Eng): for teams losing a role in restructuring, we will provide reallocation tokens to managers. that means some teams may get hiring tokens to backfill or convert to adjacent roles within a quarter.
mike_sales (Sales Lead): will there be visibility into token allocations? sales ops needs to plan territories.
Priya (Head of People): yes  managers will see allocation dashboards in Workday by next week. we'll also run a manager office hour to walk through it.
Maya (CEO): we aim to be transparent about the "why" behind each change. if something in the org map looks off, escalate to your lead and cc Priya.
all-hands-bot: poll created "Do you feel the hiring plan was explained clearly?" options: Yes / Somewhat / No
Evan (Head of Research): thanks for focusing hires on model-efficiency. small ask  can we get clarity on research KPIs used to approve hires?
Maya (CEO): good point. hires will need an owner-defined metric tied to product outcomes or cost savings (e.g., 20% KV cache reduction or 2x throughput improvement). we'll publish the approval rubric.
Tess (Hiring Ops): follow-ups I'll post after the thread: 1) link to new interview rubrics, 2) hiring priority spreadsheet (manager-only), 3) internal mobility signup form.
mike_sales (Sales Lead): appreciated. when does hiring accelerate?
Priya (Head of People): expect phased acceleration after finance signs off on Q3 budgets  likely early next month. managers should open calibrated reqs now so we have a pipeline.
Maya (CEO): final note  we're not trying to be reactive; this is a deliberate plan to invest where we get leverage. leadership office hours next Thursday for deeper questions.
all-hands-bot: reactions summary: :thumbsup: 18 / :confused: 2
